transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is… I’ve been having a hard time with a scar on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they see about me now.
Do you find yourself thinking a lot about how your scar looks, maybe feeling like it’s much worse than it really is?

Yes. I do think about it a lot. I know, logically, the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like people notice it right away. Like their eyes go straight to it, and that’s what they see about me now.
Does worrying about your scar cause you distress or make it hard for you to participate in activities like church or playing bridge?

Yes, it does. I’ve been late turning in some of my bookkeeping work because I get stuck trying to cover it or check how it looks. And I’ve skipped a few choir and theater volunteer things too, because I was too worried people would notice my wrist.
Do you believe that the scar on your wrist looks abnormal in a way that others can objectively see, even if they don’t mention it?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s objectively abnormal. I know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Have you ever felt like people are talking about your scar behind your back or making judgments about it that they haven’t actually mentioned to you?

I don’t know that I’ve thought they were talking about it behind my back exactly. It’s more that when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like their eyes go right to my wrist. I know it probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me, but in the moment it feels like that’s the first thing they notice.
Have you ever had the feeling that people are thinking negatively about your scar in ways that you can't confirm, even though they haven't said anything to you?

Yes, I guess I do. I know it’s probably not as noticeable as it feels to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I start feeling like people’s eyes go straight to my wrist. Like they’re noticing it right away and thinking something about it, even if they don’t say anything.
Do you feel that your wrist scar looks deformed or very different from how it actually is, even though others might not see it that way?

Yes… I mean, I do know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me. But it feels very different to me now. When I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep thinking everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me.
Do you find these thoughts about your scar coming up repeatedly, even when you're trying not to think about it?

Yes, it does come up again and again. I can be trying to focus on church or a bridge game, and then I’ll suddenly be thinking about my wrist. I know the scar probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me, but I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice now.
Do you ever feel like people are paying attention to your scar in a way that you just know it’s true, even if there’s no proof or they haven’t said anything?

Yes… I don’t know if I’d say I know it for sure, but it feels that way in the moment. Like at church or when I’m playing bridge, I’ll feel like people’s eyes go right to my wrist, like the scar is the first thing they notice. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but I still feel that way.
Do you ever hold onto certain beliefs about your scar being extremely noticeable or causing others to judge you, even though you've been told otherwise or have evidence that it's not true?

Yes, I do, even though part of me knows it’s probably not that obvious. I’ve been told it doesn’t look that bad, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I still feel like people notice my wrist right away. It’s like I can’t shake the feeling that it’s the first thing they see about me now.
Are you also concerned about any other parts of your body or physical features in the same way you are about your wrist scar?

No, not really. It’s mainly the scar on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like that’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Do you ever feel certain that people are noticing or judging your scar in ways that you just know are true, even though you can’t explain how you know it?

Not certain, exactly… I know I don’t have proof. But in the moment, like at church or when I’m playing bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to my wrist. I know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me, but it feels like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.
Do you believe that your wrist scar is so noticeable that it must be obvious to everyone, even though others have told you it isn’t or you can see in photos that it’s not as bad?

Yes… I mean, I know when I look at photos it probably isn’t as bad as it feels to me. And people have told me it’s not that noticeable. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I still feel like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.

Even though you know others don’t seem to notice your scar and photos show it’s not that bad, do you ever feel deep down that it’s actually more noticeable than others are letting on, like it’s hiding in plain sight or they’re just being polite?

Yes, sometimes. I know people say they don’t notice it, and in pictures it doesn’t look as bad as it feels to me. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I still get this feeling that their eyes go right to my wrist, like they’re noticing it right away and maybe just not saying anything.
Do you ever feel that, despite what people say or what you see in photos, there's some hidden truth that your scar is actually very obvious to everyone and they're just not telling you?

I wouldn’t say I’m completely sure there’s some hidden truth. I know people may just be telling me the truth, and in photos it doesn’t look as bad. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like their eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice now.
